subject: Re: Next steps — procurement path, PO vs card, & approvals mapping (FintechCo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps — procurement path, PO vs card, & approvals mapping (FintechCo)

Hi Alex / Emma —

Great to meet the team earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on procurement and commercial path: 

Recap from discovery:
- Primary use case: low-latency chat + multitenant embeddings for customer support routing (prod pilot Q2).
- Target initial commit: 6 reserved GPU instances for pilot, bump to x12 at scale.
- Key non-negotiables: SOC 2 evidence, private VPC option, and clear pricing for PO workflow.

Procurement & commercial questions we discussed (please confirm):
1) Preferred payment method: PO (Net 30) vs corporate card — you mentioned procurement prefers PO. Confirm?
2) Marketplace interest: Are you open to AWS Marketplace listing / procurement? That changes billing flow and possibly approval path.
3) Budget owner / economic buyer: Who owns the budget for this initiative (name & title)?
4) Finance sponsor & signatory path: Who in Finance / Legal signs (procurement contact, CFO, procurement portal)?
5) Timeline: Target date to have PO and contract signed for pilot?

Attachments: I attached our answered RFP excerpts that map to SOC2 / data handling.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm PO vs card and names for budget owner / signatory (can reply to this thread).
- We’ll produce a preliminary quote + SOW draft for review (Rishi will attach the SOW draft).
- If helpful, schedule a 30-min procurement call next week with your finance signatory and our legal/finance.

I’ll prepare a mutual action plan once you confirm the approval chain.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RFP-answers-FintechCo.pdf (PDF, 8 pages)
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Emma Li <emma.li@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps — procurement path, PO vs card, & approvals mapping (FintechCo)

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the RFP attachment. Quick answers below to get you unblocked: 

1) Payment method: Procurement generally prefers PO (Net 30) for projects of this size. We can do card for a short pilot but expect a PO for any committed reserved capacity.
2) Marketplace: We are interested in AWS Marketplace as a secondary path — it depends on pricing parity and whether we can get the same entitlements (VPC/private deployment).
3) Budget owner: Economic buyer is Harold Singh (CFO). He signs off on any multi-quarter reserved spend over $200k.
4) Finance sponsor / signatory: Primary finance sponsor is Emma Li (Director, Procurement) — she owns the PO flow and vendor onboarding. Final signatory for contracts will be Harold (CFO).
5) Timeline: If we start the vendor evaluation this week, procurement can issue a PO in ~3–6 weeks (depends on internal legal review).

Action items for Redwood:
- Preliminary quote for 6 GPU reserved pilot + optional AWS Marketplace pricing.
- Draft SOW and standard terms and redlines guide (we can route to our legal).
- SOC2 evidence + security questionnaire answers (attached RFP looks good).

I’m looping Harold on a planning call — Harold, I’ve cc’d you for awareness; Marissa / Rishi are from Redwood and will share the proposal & SOW.

Best,
Alex
VP Product, FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com

Subject: Draft SOW + preliminary technical notes (FintechCo pilot)

Hi Alex / Marissa —

Following Marissa’s note, attaching a draft SOW for the 6-GPU reserved pilot. Key technical/ops notes: 
- Deployment: Dedicated pool in us-west-2 with private VPC peering (we can support AWS Marketplace AMI pairing if you go that route).
- Data residency: Logs and metrics retention configurable; default retention 90 days (we can extend).
- Security: SOC2 report and vendor questionnaire answers included in the RFP attachment; we can provide more granular network diagrams on request.
- Support: Standard business-hours support + 24x7 escalation add-on.

Attachments: SOW-draft-FintechCo.docx (Word doc)

If the procurement path is PO, we’ll need the following to generate final quote for PO invoice:
- Billing entity (legal name + remit address)
- PO contact for receiving invoice
- Any mandatory PO fields (e.g., PO number field requirements)

I’ve left placeholders in the SOW for billing entity and signature block.

—Rishi

Hi Alex / Emma / Harold —

Thanks for the quick clarifications — helpful. Proposed mutual action plan & next steps so we can move procurement forward: 

Mutual action plan (proposed)
- By 2026-03-03: FintechCo to confirm billing entity + PO contact + any mandatory PO fields (Alex / Emma)
- By 2026-03-05: Redwood to send preliminary quote (PO terms) + updated SOW with billing info (Marissa / Rishi)
- Week of 2026-03-09: Procurement call with Emma + Harold, Redwood legal & finance to review contract and PO flow
- Target signature/PO issuance: by 2026-03-20 (subject to legal review)

On marketplace: we’ll include AWS Marketplace pricing in the quote as an alternate. If you prefer the Marketplace flow, note it may add a 1–2 week listing/onboarding step but simplifies recurring billing.

Action items from us (I’ll take the lead):
- Send preliminary quote and SOW (including PO invoice fields) by EOD 2026-03-05.
- Prep a short procurement FAQ (PO vs card, Marketplace implications, standard payment terms).
- Schedule procurement call for week of 2026-03-09 — can you share two 30-min windows that week that work for Emma + Harold?

If that timeline looks reasonable I’ll move forward and share the DocuSign-ready SOW once we have billing entity details.

Best,
Marissa Cole
